title: Handwriting Test for Preschool Children (HT-PRE)
author: Qin Hong
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5fmg3k6
materials: The HT-PRE was then conducted one-on-one.

steps.title: Collect participant background information
steps.instruction: Have parents complete the Children’s Basic Situation Questionnaire, gathering the child’s age, gender, medical history, and trauma history.

steps.title: Prepare individual record form
steps.instruction: Use the Individual Record Form to record any special behavior observed during testing.

steps.title: Write familiar personal information
steps.instruction: Ask the child to write, from memory, the most familiar contents: name, age, class, and Arabic numbers 1‑9 in sequence.

steps.title: Write ten two‑digit numbers
steps.instruction: Read aloud ten two‑digit numbers that have been randomly selected from a random number table; the child writes each number.

steps.title: Copy alphabet letters
steps.instruction: Present 24 alphabet letters (excluding O and I) that are randomly arranged into two lines; the child copies them sequentially.

steps.title: Copy Chinese characters
steps.instruction: Provide 12 Chinese characters containing all basic strokes and structures, selected from volumes 1–4 of the primary school textbooks, placed in a blank standard character grid for the child to copy.
